Rationale: The contract requires the vendor to maintain a written password standard, including administrative accounts with a minimum of 14 characters for length and strength. Additionally, the contract specifies salted hashing for storage and requires secure storage of passwords. These commitments meet the requirement, and there are no notable gaps or ambiguities.

The contract requires the vendor to maintain an inventory of in-scope assets (Section 9.1), review and reconcile the inventory at least quarterly and upon material changes (Section 9.2), and maintain secure configuration baselines for in-scope systems (Section 9.3). The inventory is to include at least the 'Asset ID', 'Asset type', 'Environment', 'Data sensitivity', 'Owner', 'Region', and 'Last reviewed' fields (Exhibit G (ASSET-01) Asset Inventory Minimum Fields).

Relevant Quotes: Exhibit G4. Cryptography and Secrets, ID CRYP-02 (Encrypt Company Data at rest); Security Schedule, G1. Governance and Risk Management, Requirement GOV-04 (Maintain security awareness training); Section 5.1 (Vendor will implement and maintain safeguards designed to protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Company Data)
Rationale: The contract requires annual security awareness training through Exhibit G1. Governance and Risk Management, Requirement GOV-04. Additionally, the Security Schedule, G4. Cryptography and Secrets, ID CRYP-02, requires encryption of Company Data at rest. However, the control baseline and minimum security requirements in Section 5.1 lack explicit language on annual background screening for all personnel with data access, resulting in a partially compliant determination.

Relevant Quotes: 5.1 Baseline. Vendor will implement and maintain safeguards designed to protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Company Data (...); 18. Regulatory Requests and Legal Holds Vendor will notify Company of legally binding requests for Company Data (...); 10. Secure Development and Change Management (if applicable) Vendor will maintain secure SDLC practices and change management for production changes affecting Company Data.
Rationale: Although the contract mentions safeguarding Company Data, the requirements do not explicitly state the use of TLS 1.2 or higher for all external and internal transmissions. Section 5.1 mentions a general baseline of safeguarding Company Data, but it doesn't specifically address encryption. Additionally, Section 18 and 10 refer to different types of data and processes, but they don't provide clarity on the encryption standard used for data in transit.

Relevant Quotes: Section 6.2 (MFA for privileged and production access); Section 6.7 (Administrative access via approved bastion/secure gateway); Exhibit G (AuthN/AuthZ)
Rationale: The contract explicitly mentions MFA for privileged and production access (Section 6.2), administrative access occurs only via approved bastion/secure gateway with MFA and session logging (Section 6.7), and Exhibit G provides comprehensive AuthN/AuthZ details. Although Exhibit C lists some authentication protocols, the overall contract demonstrates a clear commitment to MFA for all relevant access types.
